title: P4 — a decimal disk floor is truncated down (5.9G resolves to 5 GiB), so admission enforces a lower number than the operator wrote while reporting the value as if it were theirs

detail.file: scripts/disk_floor.py:55 (int(raw) for floats) and :66 (int(float(m.group('num')))) — the truncation; scripts/lib.sh:35-44 require_disk compares the returned integer against df's float
detail.measured: resolve --cli 5.9G -> floor_gib 5 (source cli); config default = "5.9G" -> floor_gib 5 (source config-default); --cli 5.5G -> floor_gib 5; with a df shim reporting 5.5 GB free, require_disk PASSes against the resolved 5
detail.contradicted_docstring: scripts/disk_floor.py:17-19 'Accepted values: "<int>" or "<int>G" / "<int>GiB" / "<decimal>G" ... Anything else fails closed (exit 2) rather than silently falling back to a default — a typo must not lower a floor'
detail.not_duplicate_of: CF-007 (P1, pending: the disk policy must exist and name its number) — this is a defect in the shipped resolver's input handling, reproducible without a node

reasoning:
Measured 2026-11-03 by the code-factory releng-QA lane (tick code-factory-releng-qa-2026-11-03-15-39-07) at origin/main ac30ceb, no node and no network.

(1) `scripts/disk_floor.py` accepts decimal sizes by design (docstring :17) but converts them with `int(float(...))` (:66) and `int(raw)` (:55), so a floor is truncated DOWN, never up and never refused: `resolve --cli 5.9G --explain` prints `{"role": "worker", "floor_gib": 5, "source": "cli"}` and a config `default = "5.9G"` prints the same 5 with `source: config-default`. `5.1G`, `5.5G` and `5.9G` are therefore the same policy, and 5.0-5.9 are one number.

(2) The module's own contract states the opposite intent: 'Anything else fails closed (exit 2) rather than silently falling back to a default — a typo must not lower a floor.' A truncated decimal is exactly a silent lowering, and the `source` field it prints ('cli', 'config-default') asserts the operator's value was used, which hides the substitution.

(3) The consequence reaches admission, not just the printed JSON: `require_disk` (scripts/lib.sh:35-44) compares `df`'s float free-space with the integer the resolver returned. With a `df` shim reporting 5.5 GB free and a floor requested as 5.9G, the row reads `PASS  disk — 5.5 GB free (floor 5 GB)` and the admission returns 0 — a host below the operator's floor is admitted, and the printed floor is the truncated number, so the mismatch is invisible in the very output that is supposed to make the refusal falsifiable (CF-007's premise).

(4) The same value feeds the `--apply` path (`project-node.sh:144` require_disk, `:107-113` floor resolution), so this is an acceptance decision, not a label.

(5) Not established here: which of the two repairs the project wants (preserve the decimal through a float comparison, or refuse decimals outright with exit 2). The row requires one of them plus a test, and names the docstring that has to agree.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A decimal floor never resolves below the requested number: either the value is preserved (`5.9` stays 5.9 through `require_disk`'s comparison) or it is refused with `FAIL disk-floor: ...` and exit 2. Prove with the row probe: `resolve --cli 5.9G --explain` prints a floor >= 5.9 or exits 2 with the named message.

2. Distinct decimals produce distinct enforcement: `5.1G`, `5.5G`, `5.9G` yield three different floors (or three refusals), proven by one `require_disk` arm per value against a `df` shim reporting 5.5 GB free — 5.1 PASSes, 5.9 must not.

3. A numbered `tests/selftest.sh` section asserts those arms and FAILS on the pre-fix `scripts/disk_floor.py` (paste both runs and both exit codes into the evidence artifact).

4. The docstring, `--help`, and any spec/README text quoting the accepted forms state the rounding policy the code actually implements — the sentence 'a typo must not lower a floor' is true of the shipped resolver.

5. `bash tests/selftest.sh` prints `SELFTEST: PASS`, `scripts/boardctl validate` prints `RESULT: OK`, the board parses every line with unique ids, and the closing commit is pushed with `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` = 0.
probe:
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || exit 1
p=$(mktemp -d)
printf '[disk]\ndefault = "5.9G"\n' > "$p/floor.toml"
echo "requested_floor=5.9G"
printf 'cli_5.9G      -> '; python3 scripts/disk_floor.py resolve --cli 5.9G --explain
printf 'config_5.9G   -> '; python3 scripts/disk_floor.py resolve --role worker --config "$p/floor.toml" --explain

mkdir -p "$p/bin"
printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "Filesystem 1024-blocks Used Available Capacity Mounted\n/dev/x 100 1 5767168 1%% /\n"' > "$p/bin/df"
chmod +x "$p/bin/df"
echo "--- admission arm: df reports 5.5 GB free, floor requested was 5.9 GB ---"
PATH="$p/bin:$PATH" bash -c '. ./scripts/lib.sh; FAILED=0; require_disk "$HOME" "$(python3 ./scripts/disk_floor.py resolve --cli 5.9G)"; echo "admission_rc=$?"'
